beats.trigger: ## Lecture: Access is not absorption
beats.got: nothing new; the title gives away the point, and it is my prework example.

beats.trigger: Absorption happens in other people's weeks, at their pace, for their reasons.
beats.got: Licences count as access, and people's weeks decide use. I recognise this from every rollout I have seen.

beats.trigger: The proposal got neither a yes nor a no.
beats.got: A company redesigned a value stream with agents, and leadership never decided. The story is honest and understated, and I trust it more because it is a failure.

beats.trigger: Accountability is the part with a name on it, and a name does not travel inside a folder.
beats.got: You can copy context, boundary and checks, but not the person who answers for the agent. That is a people question.

beats.trigger: Pick the one your teammate's week can take in.
beats.got: Each sharing option asks something different of the receiver: trust, fit, habit or upkeep.

beats.trigger: Somebody they trust has to have used it first and said so.
beats.got: People switch when it lands where they look, works first time, and a trusted colleague vouches for it.

beats.trigger: Have the conversation before you build anything more.
beats.got: Talk to one person before building more.

beats.trigger: Who gets your context, who gets a skill, who wants only the output, and who would use an @mention?
beats.got: Different colleagues need different forms of sharing.

beats.trigger: Access is a switch someone flips. Absorption happens in other people's weeks.

take_homes: Access is not use. Before any rollout, ask what would have to be true for one named person to switch from what they do today.
Write the people plan beside the technical plan: who owns it, who answers for it, who spreads it. A plan with unnamed roles is not finished.
Pick what to share by the outcome for the person, not by the platform we already own.

monday.move: Talk to one HR business partner about how they prepare the weekly people-metrics summary today, and ask what would have to be true for them to use an agent version. Build nothing yet.
monday.who: One HR business partner I trust
monday.stop_condition: They say the summary is not the job that hurts, or they do not trust it with employee data.
monday.blocker: Employee data in an AI tool needs the works council and the DPO. I have not asked either yet, so I will ask them before anything runs on real data.

misconception.why: I came in thinking the question was which roles go. The module shows that adoption is slow and depends on people, which gives me a more careful answer for the leadership team. It never addressed headcount, so I'm still not sure my first belief is wrong.

one_line: It's not really about agents. It's about why people don't use what you give them, and I'd say that to any HR or change leader.
